intro: Someone says the WiFi isn't working. Start with their phone number or email — most of the time the answer is already here.
demoNote: This is a demo venue with sample guests. Your own venue shows your real guests.
loadErrorTitle: We couldn't load this location just now
loadErrorBody: This is a problem reaching us, not a problem with your internet. Nothing has changed at your venue.
enterPhone: Enter the phone number or email the guest used to log in.
lookupForbidden: You don't have permission to look up guests here.
lookupFailed: We couldn't look that guest up just now.
resetDeviceCleared: Done — they're off the network and back at the login page.
resetControllerVenue: Session reset — their next sign-in starts fresh.
resetNotCleared: Session reset in our records only.
resetNotClearedBody: The router did not confirm taking their device off, so they may still be online. Ask them to forget the network and reconnect.
resetSessionOnly: Session reset — they'll sign in again from the login page.
resetSessionOnlyBody: Whether their device was taken off the network was not reported.
resetRefused: Session reset, but their device was not taken off the network.
resetRefusedBody: This venue's controller declined the request.
whoBody: Type the phone number or email they used to log in. If you don't have it, pick them from the list.
internalRefNote: Some rows show an internal reference instead of a phone number — guest sessions don't carry the number yet.
nothingToFixBody: When a guest tells you the WiFi isn't working, type their number above and we'll tell you what we can see.
resetConfirmDevice: They'll be disconnected and sent back to the login page to sign in again. Anything they're in the middle of will stop.
resetConfirmFresh: Their session ends and their next sign-in starts fresh at the login page.
resetConfirmNoDevice: We cannot take their device off this venue's network, so they may stay connected until they reconnect.
enterSite: Enter the website the guest can't open, e.g. instagram.com
siteTitle: A guest can't open one particular site?
siteControllerBody: Not something we can test from here at this venue.
siteControllerNote: Website blocking and the “try it from your router” test both run on the router itself, so they are done in that controller. The guest lookup beside this still works normally — it reads sign-in records, not your network.
siteBody: We'll check your own blocking rules first, then try it from your router.
checkingSite: Checking from your router — this takes a few seconds.
historyBody: Every test we ran, with the raw result. Useful if you're on the phone to your internet provider.
historyErrorTitle: We couldn't read back this router's history
historyErrorBody: Your earlier checks are still recorded — we just couldn't load them.
historyEmptyBody: Anything this page runs against your router is listed here.
rulesUnreadable: We couldn't read this venue's blocked-website list.
rulesUnreadableBody: The check below only covers whether the site is reachable, not whether one of your own rules blocks it.

aruba.statusNote: This comes from guests signing in, not from the access point itself. Idle can just mean nobody is connected. Wyfy can't see whether an access point is powered on.

noNetwork.title: The guest can't see the WiFi
noNetwork.step1: Check that the access point has power and its light is on.
noNetwork.step2: If the light is on and the WiFi still doesn't show, ask your Wyfy Guest contact to check the guest network.

noLoginPage.title: WiFi connects, but the login page doesn't open
noLoginPage.step1: Ask the guest to turn off mobile data and any VPN or Private DNS.
noLoginPage.step2: Ask them to forget the WiFi network, join again, and open any website.
noLoginPage.step3: If nobody gets the page, ask your Wyfy Guest contact to check the login page setup for this network.

noCode.title: The login code doesn't arrive
noCode.step1: Check the number or email they typed, then look it up above.
noCode.step2: Wait a minute and ask them to request one code. Repeated requests can be refused for a while.

noInternet.title: Signed in, but no internet
noInternet.step1: Look up the guest above: it shows whether they are blocked or their time has run out.
noInternet.step2: Ask them to turn WiFi off and on, then sign in again.
noInternet.step3: If every guest is affected, check the access point's power and ask your provider about the venue's internet line.

slow.title: The internet is slow
slow.step1: Check the guest speed limit under Guest WiFi Limits. It applies to every device on that network.
slow.step2: If there is no limit, check the venue's internet line with your provider.

oneSite.title: One website won't open
oneSite.step1: Ask the guest to try another website. If that works, the problem is probably with that site.
oneSite.step2: Wyfy can't test a website from this venue. If it fails for every guest, ask your Wyfy Guest contact.
